question: A 1991 study of death certificates found left-handers died nine years younger. What mostly explains the gap?
options: Birth stress that also shortens life
answer: Fewer left-handers among the old. Children born early in the century were often made to write with the right hand, so few elderly people called themselves left-handed, and the left-handers who died were mostly younger. Mean age at death compared generations, not risks; studies following living people forward found little or no gap.
move: Compare the dead only after asking when each group was born.
trap: Right-handed tools and cars make an accident story feel obvious.
source: Galobardes et al., Am J Public Health, 1999
